Today, tax automation has a **shared core with provider-specific adapters**, but the migration is incomplete: **Instead is the only registered adapter**. Juno still has legacy paths. GruntWorx already has a database enum value, but no entry in the adapter registry.

**Vendor-neutral ports**

The shared `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations` layer owns:

| Port | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `Authorizations::Create` | Start the selected provider’s connection ceremony. |
| `Connections::Create` | Complete authorization, select the provider, bind its external account, and displace the previous connection. |
| `Connections::Find`, `Disconnect`, `DisconnectAll` | Report or end connections, including lifecycle events affecting every provider. |
| `Connections::Renew`, `Revoke`, `VerifyGrant` | Maintain and verify grants through the provider’s client. |
| `ExportAsync` | Authorize the export, validate files against capabilities, create shared records, then delegate delivery. |
| Document services/workers | Shared upload failures, status broadcasting, reconnect recovery, and reconciliation scheduling. |
| Cleanup/merge services | Remove provider data when envelopes or firms disappear, and handle contact merges. |

For export, the boundary is explicit: the core hands the adapter a tax-preparation envelope and shared send records; the adapter decides how to deliver them. See [ExportAsync](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53).

**Registration and the adapter namespace**

[Registry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:3) contains a static mapping:

```ruby
ADAPTERS = {instead: TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead}.freeze
FEATURE_FLAGS = {instead: :tax_automations_instead}.freeze
```

A firm’s settings select its current provider. Unknown or unregistered providers raise `UnknownProviderError`. Background and cleanup operations can enumerate every registered adapter, independently of the firm’s current selection.

The effective namespace contract comes from production dispatch sites:

| Namespace member | Expected interface |
|---|---|
| `Connection` | ActiveRecord model with `.for_firm`, `.usable_for`, `.capabilities`, and the shared grant lifecycle/token interface. Background jobs also query `.connected`, `firm_id`, and `refresh_expires_at`. |
| `Client` | Constructible with a connection; supports shared token renewal/revocation. |
| `Authorizations::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, return_url)` → authorization URL. |
| `Connections::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, params)` → connection, optionally reporting `external_tenant_uuid`. |
| `ExportAsync` | `.call(user, actor, tax_preparation, tax_automation_documents:)`. |
| `Documents::ReconcileStatusesAsync` | `.call(user, actor, connection, tax_automation_document_ids:)`. |
| `DestroyForTaxPreparations` | Cleanup for specified envelopes. |
| `DestroyForFirm` | Cleanup for an entire firm. |
| `MergeForContact` | Merge provider records between contacts. |

The background reconciliation requirement is visible in [ReconcileSweepWorker](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_sweep_worker.rb:22); lifecycle requirements appear in [firm cleanup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/firms/destroy_cleanup.rb:55), [envelope cleanup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/batch_destroy.rb:49), and [contact merge](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/merge_for_contact.rb:92).

Instead’s client inherits `BaseClient`, which supplies transport infrastructure and `TokenRefreshable`. Required client hooks include `base_url`, `auth_headers`, and `vendor_error_message`; OAuth coordinates are declared through `oauth2_settings`. Thus, the current connection abstraction is vendor-neutral **within an OAuth-shaped contract**. See [Instead client](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/client.rb:3).

**The capability passport**

The passport is a **computed, class-level description of the vendor**, available without a connection row. `Connection` includes [HasCapabilities](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_capabilities.rb:3) and implements two private class methods:

- `capability_terms`: groups return types with their accepted extensions and maximum file size.
- `supported_tax_years`: computes the supported years.

The resulting `Dry::Struct` contains:

```text
terms:
  [{ return_type, accepted_file_formats, max_file_size_mb }, ...]
supported_tax_years: [...]
```

Supported return types are derived from `terms`. Terms may differ by return type. Validation rejects duplicate declarations, malformed extensions, nonpositive size limits, and years outside 2000 through next year. Missing implementations and malformed answers fail when `.capabilities` is called.

The passport drives both [export validation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:42) and the [API representation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/serializers/tax_preparation/base/tax_automations/connection_serializer.rb:57). The API exposes `tax_years` and enriched `return_types` containing `value`, `name`, personal/business `type`, `file_types`, and `file_size_limit`.

Instead currently advertises all 11 mapped IRS return types, the current year and previous two years, and one common set of file terms: PDF, CSV, DOCX, ODS, ODT, PPTX, TXT, XLSX; the configured default limit is 2000 MB. See [capability implementation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/connection.rb:68) and [defaults](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/config/settings.yml:1805).

**Data model**

| Entity | Role and identity |
|---|---|
| `FirmSettings` | One per firm; stores the selected provider and external account binding. Provider integers are `juno: 0`, `gruntworx: 1`, `instead: 2`. |
| `TaxPreparation` | Shared return envelope, still physically stored in `juno_tax_preparations`. Core identity is firm + client + optional contact + year. Holds return type and business details such as EIN. |
| Core `Document` | A send record linking a source document to an envelope, provider, and return type. Provider and return type are snapshots at send time. |
| Instead `Connection` | One grant per firm, with creator, encrypted credentials, expiries, grant state, installation UUID, and PKCE ceremony data. |
| Instead `Entity` | Vendor taxpayer handle/type, optional client/contact linkage, source, names, and synchronization/archive metadata. |
| Instead `Document` | One-to-one extension of a core send record: Instead entity, external file UUID, and path. |

The core send record owns two separate state machines:

- **Upload:** `waiting → uploading → uploaded`, with failure/reset paths.
- **Processing:** `sent`, `processing`, `processed`, `error`, `archived`, `exceeded`.

Its unique key includes **firm, envelope, source document, provider, and return type**, allowing the same source file to have distinct sends across providers or return types. See [shared send model](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:3).

Provider switching updates the settings pointer only when authorization completes successfully; existing send records retain their original provider. Reconnects also enforce the stored external-account binding. See [connection completion](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/connections/create.rb:40).

The main transitional detail is the envelope: its shared model still contains Juno associations and compatibility ransackers alongside the new direct client/contact columns. See [TaxPreparation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparation.rb:10).
